extraction.name: Geometry3K
extraction.description: A large-scale benchmark of 3,002 high-school geometry problems with dense formal language annotations for geometry problem solving.
extraction.creator: Pan Lu, Ran Gong, Shibiao Jiang, Liang Qiu, Siyuan Huang, Xiaodan Liang, Song-Chun Zhu
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was manually collected from two popular high-school textbooks available through two online digital libraries by well-trained annotators, and each problem was labeled with problem text, diagram, answer choices, correct answer, problem goal, geometry shapes, and dense formal language descriptions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Geometry problems collected from two popular textbooks for high school students across grades 6-12 via the online digital libraries McGraw-Hill and Geometryonline.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The dataset was split into train, validation, and test sets with a ratio of 0.7:0.1:0.2.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Well-trained annotators with undergraduate degrees manually collected each problem's text, diagram, four answer choices, and correct answer, and each problem was further labeled with the corresponding problem goal, geometry shapes, and dense formal language descriptions.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: The annotators were well-trained and had undergraduate degrees.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The work may inspire research in symbolic reasoning and interpretable models and facilitate education.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is challenging because less than 1% of problems can be solved without diagrams, and current parsers and solver components still fail on ambiguous annotations, multiple primitives, nested expressions, uncertain references, and complex problems with combined shapes and shaded areas.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is used as a benchmark to assess algorithms' performance on geometry problem solving, and it is split into training, validation, and test sets.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: By contrast, less than 1% of the problems in our Geometry3K dataset could be solved when the problem diagram is not provided. Inter-GPS might not find a solution because of inaccurate parsing results and the incomplete theorem set. For example, diagram parsing tends to fail if there are ambiguous annotations or multiple primitives in the diagram. It is difficult for the text parser to handle nested expressions and uncertain references. And the symbolic solver is still not capable of solving complex problems with combined shapes and shaded areas in the diagrams.
